propositions: Flat per-context bound of 100,000 chars is outgrown when individual contexts exceed it (c9f7 at 121,147 chars), and raising the bound chases a monotonically growing tail.

Recovery preflight refuses contexts that exceed a flat ceiling even when the economic product (context_chars × criteria_count) is under the ratified worst case (c9f7: 121,147 × 22 = 2.67M < 3.2M limit).
Two independent resource ceilings are conflated in _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS: a physical window limit per evidence run and an economic fan-out multiplier for recovery re-sends.
The physical ceiling must derive from the resolved verifier model's own context window rather than a hard-coded constant, so it scales with configured model capacity.

The economic ceiling should express the total recovery input product (context × criteria) directly at 3.2M chars rather than splitting arbitrarily per-axis, allocating headroom where real tickets need it.
Refusal at recovery preflight must remain visible and elision-free, with diagnostics showing context size, derived limit, criteria count, product, and product limit.
